answer:
Hypothesis (data-grounded, answering the question):

In a PCA on the twelve forms of capital — hatchets/swords, daggers, house size, copper/gold, amber, monument count, hoards/deposits, sickles, axes/celts, monument size, pottery form and pottery decoration — computed across the hundred-year time slices (n=39 bins, 4300–500 BCE), the first principal component (PC1; explains ≈30% of the variance) characterizes BOTH the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) as sitting at the NEGATIVE (low) pole of the component. PC1 is a capital/complexity gradient dominated by copper/gold (+0.41), pottery decoration (+0.38), hoards (+0.34), hatchets/swords (+0.30) and daggers (+0.27).

- Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE): the deepest, most negative part of the Neolithic on PC1 — mean ≈ −1.4, with a trough of ≈ −1.8 around 3200–3000 BCE (scores: 3400 −0.58, 3300 −1.28, 3200 −1.76, 3100 −1.47, 3000 −1.78).
- Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE): also negative on average (mean ≈ −1.1) but LESS extreme than the Middle Neolithic, and it shows a clear rising/recovering trend within the period, climbing from ≈ −1.6 (2900 BCE) toward ≈ −0.4 (2300 BCE).

So on PC1 the Middle Neolithic is the more negative (lower) of the two phases, while the Younger Neolithic — still below zero — trends upward toward it. Positive PC1 scores (the high-capital/complexity end of the gradient) do not appear until later: the Late Neolithic (~1900 BCE) and especially the Bronze Age (PC1 up to ≈ +4.4). Contextually, the pollen landscape-openness PC1 (a separate Belau/Woserin indicator) is also negative in both periods (MN ≈ −0.48, YN ≈ −0.56, i.e. a relatively closed landscape), consistent with a pre-“complexity” Neolithic. Note: the ABSOLUTE sign of PC1 is a convention (here fixed so the high-complexity Bronze Age is positive); the relative Middle-vs-Younger Neolithic comparison is sign-invariant.

Robustness (reported separately, assumption-dependent): aggregating the 12 forms into conceptual capital groups (economic/social/cultural/symbolic/domestic — an ASSUMED, undocumented mapping) and running PCA on the group means gives a materially different, noisier picture (MN ≈ +1.1, YN ≈ −0.2, r≈0.49 with the 12-form PC1). Because this rests on an undocumented grouping plus a within-group averaging step, it is treated only as a sensitivity check and does not override the primary 12-form result.

payload.hypothesis: In a PCA on the twelve forms of capital (hatchets/swords, daggers, house size, copper/gold, amber, monument count, hoards/deposits, sickles, axes/celts, monument size, pottery form, pottery decoration) computed in hundred-year time slices, PC1 (≈30% of variance; a capital/complexity gradient led by copper/gold, pottery decoration, hoards, hatchets/swords and daggers) places both the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) at the NEGATIVE (low) pole. The Middle Neolithic is the most negative of the Neolithic (mean ≈ -1.4, trough ≈ -1.8 around 3200-3000 BCE); the Younger Neolithic is also negative on average (mean ≈ -1.1) but less extreme and rising/recovering across the period (≈ -1.6 at 2900 BCE toward ≈ -0.4 at 2300 BCE). Thus the Middle Neolithic is the lower/more-negative phase and the Younger Neolithic, still below zero, trends upward toward it. Positive PC1 (high capital/complexity) only emerges later (Late Neolithic ~1900 BCE, especially the Bronze Age). The absolute PC1 sign is a convention (fixed so the Bronze Age is positive); the MN-vs-YN relative comparison is sign-invariant.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/capital.csv (decimal=','); 39 rows = one 100-year bin each, 4300-500 BCE, 12 Z-scored forms of capital; 0 missing, 0 duplicate BCE. Verified capital.csv == time_series_data.csv *_inter at century marks. 2) Defined periods from the 'group' column: MN={3400..3000} (3400-3000 BCE, 5 bins), SG/YN={2900..2300} (2900-2300 BCE, 7 bins) — matches the question. Binning convention: each row labels a 100-y bin by its older/start year; period assignment comes from the group labels so the within-bin boundary convention does not matter. 3) Standardized each of the 12 variables to mean 0/std 1 (ddof=1) -> PCA on the correlation matrix via SVD (numpy). 4) Fixed PC1 sign toward greater capital/complexity: flipped so the mean PC1 of the Bronze Age bins (OBA+YBA) is positive; documented that absolute sign is a convention and the relative comparison is sign-invariant. 5) Extracted PC1 scores per bin; compared MN vs YN in mean, range (min/max) and within-period linear trend; reported explained variance and PC1 loadings. 6) Context: pollen landscape-openness PC1 (MEAN / SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) for both periods. 7) Robustness: aggregated the 12 forms into assumed conceptual capital groups (economic/social/cultural/symbolic/domestic), PCA on group means, compared MN vs YN. Script: analysis_pca_capital.py (re-run reproduces all figures).
